title: Canada Wildfires Update — Sep 25, 2026
summary: The out-of-control Mount Jack fire west of Sooke, BC grew to 276 hectares as of September 24 and was determined human-caused; heavy smoke blanketed Greater Victoria and grounded helicopter bucketing for parts of the day, though roughly 60 personnel remain assigned and no evacuation orders or alerts have been issued. It is now one of only two wildfires still classified out of control provincewide, as BC's active count eased to 100 fires from 105 two days earlier. The Northwest Territories' season effectively wound down — its active fire count collapsed from 79 to just 7 (5 out of control, 2 under control), with 282 of the season's 289 fires now declared out. The Ainslie Creek fire near Merritt grew modestly to 69,705 hectares while remaining classified as held. No new deaths, evacuation orders, or economic developments were identified this cycle.

title: Canada Wildfires Update — Sep 21, 2026
summary: The 2026 season's quiet fall wind-down continued through the week of September 14-21 with no verified new fire starts, evacuation-order changes, or deaths. Northwestern Ontario's active count remains near its season low (31 on Sept 18, ticking to 32 on Sept 19 after the small Nipigon 112 start); BC's Bald Range, Pear Lake and Ainslie Creek fires remain 'under control' or 'being held'. CIFFC's September 16 national situation report — the season's final weekly report, with preparedness at Level 2 and no priority fires — still stands as the most current official national assessment; a full season summary is expected later this fall. No newer official figures, fire starts, or evacuation changes were found in this cycle's research despite targeted searches for September 17, 20 and 21 developments.

title: Canada Wildfires Update — Sep 18, 2026
summary: The Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre lowered the National Preparedness Level from 3 to 2 in its September 16 national situation report — the last weekly report of the 2026 season — citing no remaining priority fires nationally and fire count/area burned near or below the 10-year average. CIFFC will publish a full season summary later in the fall, with weekly reporting resuming in spring 2027. This marks the effective wind-down of the acute phase of the season: the Rinker Lake Complex in Northwestern Ontario remains formally not under control but with low activity, while BC's Bald Range, Pear Lake and Ainslie Creek fires all remain in 'under control' or 'being held' status. No new deaths, evacuation orders, or significant fire starts were identified this cycle.

title: Canada Wildfires Update — Sep 16, 2026
summary: Northwestern Ontario's active fire count kept falling through mid-September — 45 on Sept 13 and a season-low 30 by Sept 15 — with no new starts confirmed all week and the region's fire danger rating dropping to low as fall weather sets in. The Rinker Lake Complex (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34/35) remains not under control, though activity has stayed low. Nationally, the human toll continued easing sharply: Indigenous Services Canada's evacuation dashboard shows just 17 First Nations communities impacted by wildfire as of Sept 14 (16 BC, 1 Saskatchewan, 1 Ontario), 5 under active evacuation, and 178 individuals displaced — down from 4,294 evacuees across 25 communities on Aug 18. No new deaths, evacuation orders, or fire starts were identified this cycle.

title: Canada Wildfires Update — Sep 4, 2026
summary: Canada's season-to-date total reached 5,248 fires and 4,492,283 hectares burned as of August 31, up from 4,793 fires and 4.1M hectares on August 18. In British Columbia, the Pear Lake fire (166,132 ha) and the Ainslie Creek/Brunswick Creek complex near Merritt lost their 'wildfire of note' status on September 3 as growth stalled, while the Bald Range fire near Summerland had its area restriction order rescinded September 4 as activity decreased. Northwestern Ontario's active fire count climbed to 62 after nine small new starts over September 2–3 (Kenora 35, Red Lake 28, Nipigon 108, four Fort Frances fires and Thunder Bay 86), though the Rinker Lake Complex remains not under control at 377,240 combined hectares. No new deaths or evacuation orders were identified this cycle.

title: Canada Wildfires Update — Sep 2, 2026
summary: Northwestern Ontario's active wildfire count eased to 56 as of September 1, down from 59 in late August, with no new fires confirmed; the Rinker Lake Complex (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34 and Dryden 35 — a combined 377,198 hectares) remains not under control despite low fire activity. In the Northwest Territories, the season's cumulative total climbed to 288 fires and 1,694,001 hectares as of September 2, with 219 fires still active (210 out of control, 3 held, 6 under control) — more than a quarter of Canada's national burn area this season. No new deaths, evacuation orders, or economic developments were identified this cycle.

title: Canada Wildfires Update — Aug 31, 2026
summary: British Columbia's Pear Lake fire, the season's second-largest, grew to 166,111 hectares as of August 30, a modest 182-hectare gain overnight as crews worked planned ignitions and containment lines near Big Bar Mountain. In Northwestern Ontario, two small new fires — Kenora 34 near Sioux Narrows and Dryden 66 at Blue Lake Provincial Park — were confirmed August 31, though the region's active total held at 59 as other fires were closed out; the Rinker Lake Complex (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34, Dryden 35), now a combined 377,198 hectares, remains not under control despite low activity. No new deaths, evacuation orders, or economic developments were identified this cycle.

title: Canada Wildfires Update — Aug 29, 2026
summary: British Columbia ended its provincial wildfire state of emergency on August 27, two days ahead of the scheduled extension, after officials determined the declaration's powers were no longer needed even as roughly 206 wildfires continue burning across the province. The Bald Range fire near Summerland held at 25,185 hectares as weekend rain reached the fireline for the first time since it broke out, prompting further evacuation-order rescissions near Agur Lake and on Bathville Road. In Northwestern Ontario, evacuees from Eabametoong, Gull Bay and Lac Des Mille Lacs First Nations have all returned home, even as three small new fires pushed the region's active count to 59 and the Thunder Bay 36-anchored Rinker Lake Complex remains not under control.

title: Canada Wildfires Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: Federal ministers reported 4,793 fires and over 4.1 million hectares burned nationally as of August 18, with 582 wildfires still active (31 out of control) and roughly 11,000 people still under evacuation order out of ~23,000 evacuated this season. Evacuation orders eased in Peachland (Aug 14) and Summerland (Aug 18) as the Bald Range fire calms, while a previously undocumented human-caused fire, Bradley Creek near Vernon, burned over 2,600 hectares in early August before being held. 8,600 Indigenous people have been affected across 25 First Nations communities this season.
